round: r39 (C1, seat P1) — closes r38 R1-D1 (the scope-out laundering hole)
why: This file is the AUTHORITATIVE scope-out set. The comparator reads it from here, never from the payload under test, so a builder cannot make a check leave the join by self-declaration: adding a row here is a separate committed edit, and the payload's own declaration must be a subset of this set. Every row below additionally has to carry a probe the comparator can recompute blind (see 'probe_contract'), so a scope-out whose blocker is false fails closed.

probe_contract.census_rule: target = an absolute path to a substrate root. The driver recomputes, over every *.jsonl under target: session_files (count), files_with_skills_block, candidate_blocks (a '<skills>' occurrence with a later '</skills>'), and then picks the catalogue block under five blind-plausible selection rules (newest file mtime, newest embedded ISO stamp, first in scan order, last in scan order, newest with a non-empty entry list), recording each rule's entry count in 'rule_totals'. The payload's declared observable must equal this exactly; the row only stays scoped out when the rules disagree (distinct_totals has more than one value) and the surface is non-vacuous.
probe_contract.why_this_shape: A substring sweep for the rule's own literals was tried first and rejected: the carrier is this lane's own session tree, so its transcripts quote the rule's text and the sweep fails the true rows (the driver's first live run exited 2 on exactly that). Reading structure, never prose, is the sound form.
probe_contract.false_blocker_classes: the payload declares an observable that recomputation does not reproduce; the carrier is empty or carries no candidate block; every blind-plausible rule lands on one total (the row would be derivable blind); the probe is missing, non-dict, or targets a non-absolute path.

omp.catalogue.found.reason: the catalogue carrier's selection rule (which session-jsonl <skills> block is *the* catalogue: the newest qualifying block with at least min(10, len(known)) entries, matched line-by-line against the skill cache) is inside the harness's own authored scope; this instrument's substrate set does not carry it, so re-deriving the row blind would be guessing.
